title.zh: 第二十七 百官四 執金吾 太子太傅 大長秋 太子少傅 將作大匠 城門校尉 北軍中候 司隸校尉
title.raw: 第二十七 百官四 執金吾 太子太傅 大長秋 太子少傅 將作大匠 城門校尉 北軍中候 司隸校尉 Volume 117: Officials Part Four

sentences.zh: 志第二十七 百官四

translations.literal: Treatise twenty-seven: Officials, part four.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 27: The Bureaucracy, Part Four.

sentences.zh: 执金吾 太子太传 大长秋 太子少傅 将作大匠 城门校尉 北军中候 司隶校尉

translations.literal: Bearer of the gilded mace; grand tutor of the heir; grand prolonger of autumn; junior tutor of the heir; master artisan; colonel of the gates; middle commandant of the northern army; colonel director of retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The Bearer of the Gilded Mace, the heir's grand tutor, the empress's chamberlain, the heir's junior tutor, the master of works, the colonel of the gates, the northern-army middle commandant, and the colonel director of retainers.

sentences.zh: 城门校尉北军中候司隶校尉

translations.literal: Colonel of the gates, middle commandant of the northern army, colonel director of retainers.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of the gates, the northern-army middle commandant, and the colonel director of retainers.

translations.literal: One bearer of the gilded mace, salary of two thousand piculs at the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: The Bearer of the Gilded Mace was a single post at two thousand piculs, middle rate.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宫外戒司非常水火之事。

translations.literal: Original note says: He is charged with outside the palace alerting and controlling unusual matters of fire and water.
translations.idiomatic: He patrolled outside the palace walls, watched for emergencies, and dealt with fires, floods, and other crises.

sentences.zh: 月三绕行宫外，及主兵器。

translations.literal: Each month three circuits are made around outside the palace, and he is also in charge of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Each month his men circled the palace perimeter three times, and he also controlled the armory.

translations.literal: "Wu" is like "imperial chariot."
translations.idiomatic: The word wu in the title is glossed as being akin to "imperial equipage," that is, imperial guard.

translations.literal: One assistant, salary comparable to one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He had one assistant at the thousand-picul level.

translations.literal: Two hundred cavalry in red-brown.
translations.idiomatic: Two hundred mounted guards in the brown riding coats served under him.

translations.literal: Original note says: They have no rank; their sustenance is comparable to clerks' salaries.
translations.idiomatic: They held no formal rank but were fed at rates similar to clerical stipends.

translations.literal: One director of the arsenal, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The capital arsenal director held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of weapons.
translations.idiomatic: He stored and issued arms.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There was one assistant.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the bearer of the gilded mace.
translations.idiomatic: The foregoing offices reported to the Bearer of the Gilded Mace.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：本有式道、左右中候三人，六百石。

translations.literal: Original note says: Originally there were three middle commandants of the model road, left, right, and center, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: There had originally been three six-hundred-picul commandants who cleared the route for the imperial train.

sentences.zh: 车驾出，掌在前清道，还持麾至宫门，宫门乃开。

translations.literal: When the chariot train goes out, they are in charge ahead of clearing the road; returning, they hold the banner to the palace gate, and only then does the palace gate open.
translations.idiomatic: On outings they rode ahead to clear the streets; on the return they carried the signal banner to the gate before the doors would open.

sentences.zh: 中兴但一人，又不常置，每出，以郎兼式道候，事已罢，不复属执金吾。

translations.literal: At the restoration there was only one person, and moreover it was not constantly established; each time there was an outing, gentlemen took concurrent duty as model-road commandants; when the affair was finished, they were dismissed and no longer belonged to the bearer of the gilded mace.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration only one such post remained, and it was often left vacant; gentlemen were temporarily detailed as route commandants for each procession, then released and no longer under the Bearer of the Gilded Mace.

sentences.zh: 又省中垒、寺互、都船令、丞、尉及左右京辅都尉。

translations.literal: Further abolished were the central rampart, temple mutual, capital boats director, assistants, commandants, and left and right metropolitan auxiliary commandants.
translations.idiomatic: The central bastion, prison liaison, capital boat pool, and the left and right metropolitan auxiliary commands were also cut.

sentences.zh: 太子太傅一人，中二千石。

translations.literal: One grand tutor of the heir, salary of two thousand piculs at the middle grade.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's grand tutor was a single minister at two thousand piculs, middle rate.

translations.literal: Original note says: His duty is to assist and instruct the heir.
translations.idiomatic: His role was to guide and teach the crown prince.

translations.literal: Rites are as for a teacher; he does not head official subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He was honored like a tutor but commanded no separate bureaucracy.

translations.literal: One grand prolonger of autumn, two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's chamberlain, the grand prolonger of autumn, held two thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Inherited from Qin's general who goes; eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The office descended from the Qin "general who goes"; it was held by a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 景帝更为大长秋，或用士人。

translations.literal: Emperor Jing changed it to grand prolonger of autumn; sometimes literati were used.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jing renamed it grand prolonger of autumn and occasionally appointed a civil official.

sentences.zh: 中兴常用宦者，职掌奉宣中宫命。

translations.literal: At the restoration eunuchs were commonly used; the duty is to receive and proclaim the commands of the middle palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration eunuchs normally held the post and conveyed the empress's orders.

sentences.zh: 凡给赐宗亲，及宗亲当谒见者关通之，中宫出则从。

translations.literal: As for all grants and gifts to imperial kin, and imperial kin who ought to have audience, he links and communicates them; when the middle palace goes out, he follows.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged stipends for the imperial clan, passed in kinsmen who sought audience, and accompanied the empress when she left the palace.

translations.literal: One assistant, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He had one assistant at six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant was a eunuch.

translations.literal: One steward of the middle palace, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's chief steward held one thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The steward was a eunuch.

translations.literal: He is in charge of driving.
translations.idiomatic: He managed the empress's carriage horses and drivers.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：太仆，秩二千石，中兴省「太」，减秩千石，以属长秋。

translations.literal: Original note says: Grand coachman, rank two thousand piculs; at the restoration "grand" was removed, rank was reduced by one thousand piculs, and it was placed under the prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The post had been the grand coachman at two thousand piculs; the restored Han dropped the word "grand," cut the salary by one thousand piculs, and subordinated it to the chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 中宫谒者令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: One director of ushers of the middle palace, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the empress's ushers held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He was a eunuch.

translations.literal: Three ushers of the middle palace, four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Three palace ushers served at four hundred piculs each.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: They were eunuchs.

translations.literal: They are in charge of reporting memorials within.
translations.idiomatic: They transmitted memorials to and from the empress's quarters.

translations.literal: Five masters of writing of the middle palace, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Five secretariat clerks for the empress's household held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: They were eunuchs.

translations.literal: They are in charge of documents within.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the empress's correspondence and records.

sentences.zh: 中宫私府令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: One director of the private treasury of the middle palace, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the empress's private treasury held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The director was a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 主中藏币帛诸物，裁衣被补浣者皆主之。

translations.literal: He is in charge of goods stored within of silks and coins and the various things; cutting garments and bedding and those who patch and wash—all are under him.
translations.idiomatic: He stored silk and valuables for the harem and oversaw tailors, menders, and laundresses.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There was one assistant.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant was a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 中宫永巷令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: One director of the Everlasting Lane of the middle palace, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The warden of the empress's Everlasting Lane held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The warden was a eunuch.

translations.literal: He is in charge of palace women.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised palace women attached to the empress.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There was one assistant.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant was a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 中宫黄门冗从仆射一人，六百石。

translations.literal: One supervisor of supernumerary followers among attendants at the Yellow Gates of the middle palace, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The chief of the empress's supernumerary Yellow Gate escorts held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He was a eunuch.

translations.literal: He is in charge of supernumerary followers among attendants at the Yellow Gates Within.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the empress's extra inner Yellow Gate attendants.

translations.literal: One director of offices of the middle palace, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The superintendent of the empress's compound offices held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He was a eunuch.

translations.literal: He is in charge of requests to offices of the middle palace and the count of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: He processed petitions and gate clearances for the empress's bureaus and kept count of the emperor's visits to her quarters.

sentences.zh: 女骑六人，丞、复道丞各一人。

translations.literal: Six female riders; one assistant and one assistant of the covered walk, each one person.
translations.idiomatic: There were six mounted female guards, one deputy, and one deputy for the elevated corridors.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: These deputies were eunuchs.

translations.literal: The assistant of the covered walk is in charge of the covered passages within.
translations.idiomatic: The elevated-walk deputy maintained the palace skyways and galleries.

translations.literal: One chief of medicine of the middle palace, four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The empress's chief apothecary held four hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: Eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: He was a eunuch.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the grand prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: The foregoing offices belonged to the empress's chamberlain.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：承秦，有詹事一人，位在长秋上，亦宦者，主中诸官。

translations.literal: Original note says: Inherited from Qin, there was one superintendent of the heir, position above the prolonger of autumn, also a eunuch, in charge of the various offices within.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin there had been a eunuch superintendent of the heir ranking above the chamberlain and overseeing inner-court agencies.

sentences.zh: 成帝省之，以其职并长秋。

translations.literal: Emperor Cheng abolished it and merged its duties into the prolonger of autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Cheng abolished it and folded its functions into the grand prolonger of autumn.

sentences.zh: 是后皇后当法驾出，则中谒、中宦者职吏权兼詹事奉引，讫罢。

translations.literal: After this, when the empress ought to go out with the regulated chariot train, then inner ushers and inner eunuch duty clerks concurrently by authority act as superintendent leading the train; when finished, they are dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, when the empress rode in state, inner ushers and eunuch clerks temporarily doubled as superintendents to lead the cortège, then stood down.

sentences.zh: 宦者诛后，尚书选兼职吏一人奉引云。

translations.literal: After the eunuchs were executed, the masters of writing selected one concurrent-duty clerk to lead the train, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: After the eunuch purges the Secretariat picked a part-time clerk to lead the train instead.

sentences.zh: 其中长信、长乐宫者，置少府一人，职如长秋，及余吏皆以宫名为号，员数秩次如中宫。

translations.literal: As for those of enduring faith and perpetual joy palaces, one privy treasurer is established; duties are as the prolonger of autumn, and the remaining clerks all take the palace name as title; quotas, numbers, ranks, and order are as the middle palace.
translations.idiomatic: At Changxin and Changle a privy treasurer was appointed like the chamberlain, and staff took titles from the palace name with the same ranks as the empress's household.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：帝祖母称长信宫，故有长信少府，长乐少府，位在长秋上，及职吏皆宦者，秩次如中宫。

translations.literal: Original note says: The emperor's grandmother was titled enduring faith palace; therefore there was enduring faith privy treasurer, perpetual joy privy treasurer, position above the prolonger of autumn, and duty clerks were all eunuchs; ranks and order as the middle palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's grandmother took the title Changxin palace, hence Changxin and Changle privy treasurers outranked the chamberlain; their eunuch staff mirrored the empress's establishment.

sentences.zh: 长乐又有卫尉，仆为太仆，皆二千石，在少府上。

translations.literal: Perpetual joy also had a commandant of the guards; the steward was grand coachman; all were two thousand piculs, above the privy treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: Changle also had its own commandant of guards and a grand coachman at two thousand piculs, both senior to the privy treasurer.

translations.literal: When she dies, then they are abolished; not constantly established.
translations.idiomatic: Those offices were abolished at her death and were not permanent.

translations.literal: Junior tutor of the heir, two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The heir's junior tutor held two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：亦以辅导为职，悉主太子官属。

translations.literal: Original note says: Also his duty is to assist and instruct; he wholly heads the heir's official subordinates.
translations.idiomatic: He too instructed the crown prince but actually commanded the heir's entire staff.

translations.literal: One director of the heir's rotation of watches, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's master of the watch rotation held one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主庶子、舍人更直，职似光禄。

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of cadet sons and attendants rotating duty; duties resemble those of the superintendent of the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He scheduled rotating duty for the prince's cadets and attendants, much like the superintendent of the palace did for gentlemen.

translations.literal: Cadet sons of the heir, four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's cadet sons were ranked at four hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：无员，如三署中郎。

translations.literal: Original note says: There is no fixed quota; they are like gentlemen of the interior of the three bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Their number was not fixed; they corresponded to gentlemen of the interior in the three corps.

translations.literal: Attendants of the heir, two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's attendants held two hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：无员，更直宿卫，如二署郎中。

translations.literal: Original note says: There is no fixed quota; they rotate duty standing night guard; they are like gentlemen of the interior of the two bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: There was no fixed quota; they stood rotating night watch like gentlemen of the interior in the two corps.

translations.literal: One steward of the heir's household, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's major-domo held one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主仓穀饮食，职似司农、少府。

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of granaries, grain, drink, and food; duties resemble those of the minister of finance and privy treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: He ran the heir's granaries and kitchens like a miniature minister of finance and privy treasurer.

translations.literal: One director of the heir's granary, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's granary director held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of granaries and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He managed stored grain for the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 太子食官令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: One director of the heir's food office, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's catering director held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of drink and food.
translations.idiomatic: He supplied the heir's table.

translations.literal: One steward of the heir, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's coachman ranked at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主车马，职如太仆。

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of chariots and horses; duties are as the grand coachman.
translations.idiomatic: He handled the heir's stables and carriages like the imperial grand coachman.

translations.literal: One chief of the heir's stables, four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The chief groom of the heir's stables held four hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of chariots and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw the heir's horses and vehicles.

translations.literal: Gate grandee of the heir, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's gate grandee held six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：《旧注》云职比郎将。

translations.literal: Original note says: The old note says duties are comparable to a captain of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: An old commentary compares the post to a captain of the guard.

sentences.zh: 旧有左右户将，别主左右户直郎，建武以来省之。

translations.literal: Formerly there were left and right household generals, separately in charge of left and right household gentlemen on duty; from Jianwu onward they were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly left and right household captains had commanded the door guards, but Emperor Guangwu abolished them.

translations.literal: Palace cadets of the heir, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's palace cadets held six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：员五人，职如侍中。

translations.literal: Original note says: Quota of five persons; duties are like gentlemen-in-attendance.
translations.idiomatic: There were five posts, analogous to gentlemen-in-attendance at court.

translations.literal: Groomsmen who wash the horses of the heir, salary comparable to six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's grooms-of-the-stirrup were ranked at six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：《旧注》云员十六人，职如谒者。

translations.literal: Original note says: The old note says quota of sixteen persons; duties are like ushers.
translations.idiomatic: Old notes give sixteen men with duties like court ushers.

sentences.zh: 太子出，则当直者在前导威仪。

translations.literal: When the heir goes out, then those on duty go ahead in front leading deportment.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir left the palace, those on duty rode ahead to clear the way and display his train.

translations.literal: One inner shield of the heir, four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's inner shield commander held four hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of encircling guard and patrol.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the heir's close escort and patrols around the residence.

translations.literal: One guard leader of the heir, four hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince's guard captain held four hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of gate guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the guards at the heir's gates.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the junior tutor of the heir.
translations.idiomatic: The offices listed above reported to the heir's junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：凡初即位，未有太子，官属皆罢，唯舍人不省，领属少府。

translations.literal: Original note says: Whenever one first ascends the throne and there is not yet an heir, official subordinates are all dismissed; only attendants are not reduced; they are led and belong to the Privy Treasurer.
translations.idiomatic: When a new emperor had not yet named an heir, the heir's bureaucracy was disbanded except for attendants, who stayed on under the Privy Treasurer.

translations.literal: One master artisan, two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The master of works was a single minister at two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：承秦，曰将作少府，景帝改为将作大匠。

translations.literal: Original note says: Inherited from Qin, called privy treasurer of works; Emperor Jing changed it to master artisan.
translations.idiomatic: The office came from Qin as the privy treasurer of works; Emperor Jing renamed it master of works.

sentences.zh: 掌修作宗庙、路寝、宫室、陵园木土之功，并树桐梓之类列于道侧。

translations.literal: He is in charge of repair and construction of ancestral temples, route resting chamber, palaces, and mausoleum parks, works of timber and earth, and also planting paulownia, catalpa, and the like arrayed beside the roads.
translations.idiomatic: He built and repaired imperial temples, inner halls, palaces, and mausoleum parks, and lined roadsides with paulownia and catalpa.

translations.literal: One assistant, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: He had one assistant at six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: One director of the left works camp, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the left convict-labor camp held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of left work convicts.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised convict laborers assigned to the left camp.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There was one assistant.

translations.literal: One director of the right works camp, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The director of the right convict-labor camp held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of right work convicts.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised convict laborers assigned to the right camp.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There was one assistant.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the master artisan.
translations.idiomatic: These offices were under the master of works.

sentences.zh: 城门校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel of the gates, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of the gates was ranked at two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌雒阳城门十二所。

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of the twelve gates of Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the twelve gates of Luoyang.

translations.literal: One major, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: His chief of staff held one thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of soldiers at the gates.
translations.idiomatic: The major commanded the gate garrisons.

translations.literal: For each gate one gatekeeper, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Each gate had a warden at six hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：雒阳城十二门，其正南一门曰平城门，北宫门属卫尉。

translations.literal: Original note says: Luoyang city has twelve gates; the one due south is called Pingcheng Gate; the north palace gate belongs to the commandant of the guards.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang had twelve gates; the southernmost was Pingcheng Gate, while the north palace gate came under the commandant of the guards.

sentences.zh: 其余上西门，雍门，广阳门，津门，小苑门，开阳门，粍门，中东门，上东门，穀门，夏门，凡十二门。

translations.literal: The rest: Upper West Gate, Yong Gate, Guangyang Gate, Ferry Gate, Small Garden Gate, Kaiyang Gate, Haomen, Central East Gate, Upper East Gate, Grain Gate, Summer Gate—in all twelve gates.
translations.idiomatic: The other eleven gates were Upper West, Yong, Guangyang, Ferry, Small Garden, Kaiyang, Haomen, Central East, Upper East, Grain, and Summer; with Pingcheng Gate they made twelve.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the colonel of the gates.
translations.idiomatic: These posts belonged to the colonel of the gates.

translations.literal: One middle commandant of the northern army, six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The middle commandant of the northern army held six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of supervising the five camps.
translations.idiomatic: He inspected the five northern-army camps.

sentences.zh: 屯骑校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel of garrison cavalry, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of garrison cavalry was ranked at two thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of standing guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the camp's palace guard detachment.

translations.literal: One major, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Each camp had a major at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 越骑校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel of barbarian cavalry, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of Wuyue cavalry held rank at two thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of standing guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded that camp's guard troops.

translations.literal: One major, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: There was one major at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 步兵校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel of foot soldiers, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of foot soldiers held two thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of standing guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded the foot camp's guards.

translations.literal: One major, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: There was one major at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 长水校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel of long-water, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of the Long Water Hu cavalry held two thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of standing guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded that camp's guard detachment.

sentences.zh: 司马、胡骑司马各一人，千石。

translations.literal: One major and one major of Hu cavalry, each one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: There were a camp major and a Hu-cavalry major, each at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宿卫，主乌桓骑。

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of standing guard; he is in charge of Wuhuan cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The camp provided palace guard and included Wuhuan horsemen.

sentences.zh: 射声校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel of archers who sound the shot, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel of hidden archers held two thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Original note says: He is in charge of standing guard soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded that camp's guard archers.

translations.literal: One major, one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: There was one major at one thousand piculs.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the middle commandant of the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: These five colonels answered to the northern-army middle commandant.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：旧有中垒校尉，领北军营垒之事。

translations.literal: Original note says: Formerly there was a colonel of the central rampart, in charge of northern army camp rampart affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly a colonel of the central bastion had overseen the northern camps' fortifications.

sentences.zh: 有胡骑、虎贲校尉，皆武帝置。

translations.literal: There were colonels of Hu cavalry and tiger-rushers; all were established by Emperor Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu had also created separate Hu-cavalry and tiger-rushers colonels.

sentences.zh: 中兴省中垒，但置中候，以监五营。

translations.literal: At the restoration the central rampart was abolished; only the middle commandant was established, in order to supervise the five camps.
translations.idiomatic: The restored Han abolished the central bastion colonel and used only the middle commandant to supervise the five camps.

translations.literal: Hu cavalry was merged into long-water.
translations.idiomatic: The Hu-cavalry colonelcy was merged into the Long Water command.

translations.literal: Tiger-rushers were in charge of light chariots; merged into sounding-the-shot.
translations.idiomatic: The tiger-rushers' light chariots were folded into the hidden-archers regiment.

translations.literal: As for middle two thousand piculs, assistants are comparable to one thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers at two thousand piculs middle rate had assistants at one thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 真二千石，丞、长史六百石。

translations.literal: True two thousand piculs: assistants and chief clerks six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: True two-thousand-picul posts had assistants and chief clerks at six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Comparable to two thousand piculs: assistants comparable to six hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Two-thousand-picul nominal ranks had assistants at six hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Directors and chancellors one thousand piculs; assistants and commandants four hundred piculs;
translations.idiomatic: County magistrates and kingdom chancellors at one thousand piculs had assistants and commandants at four hundred;

translations.literal: Those at six hundred piculs: assistants and commandants three hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: at six hundred piculs the deputies and commandants were at three hundred.

sentences.zh: 长、相四百石及三百石，丞、尉皆二百石。

translations.literal: Chiefs and chancellors at four hundred piculs and three hundred piculs: assistants and commandants all two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Magistrates and chancellors at four hundred or three hundred piculs had assistants and commandants at two hundred.

sentences.zh: 诸侯、公主家丞，秩皆比百石。

translations.literal: Household assistants of marquises and princesses: ranks all comparable to one hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards of princely and princess households were ranked at about one hundred piculs.

sentences.zh: 诸边鄣塞尉、诸陵校尉长，皆二百石。

translations.literal: Commandants of the various border stockades and passes, colonels and chiefs of the various mausolea: all two hundred piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier blockhouse commandants and mausoleum wardens held two hundred piculs.

translations.literal: Those with constant precedent do not have rank written.
translations.idiomatic: Established posts with fixed precedent are not given explicit salary grades here.

sentences.zh: 司隶校尉一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: One colonel director of retainers, salary comparable to two thousand piculs.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel director of retainers was ranked at two thousand piculs.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：孝武帝初置，持節，掌察举百官以下，及京师近郡犯法者。

translations.literal: Original note says: Emperor Wu at first established it; he held the staff of authority; he is in charge of investigating and reporting all officials downward and those who violate the law in the capital region and neighboring commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu first created the post with a credential baton to impeach capital officials and wrongdoers in the home commanderies around Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 元帝去節，成帝省，建武中复置，并领一州。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan removed the staff; Emperor Cheng abolished it; in the Jianwu era it was restored and also headed one province.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan stripped the baton; Emperor Cheng abolished the office; Emperor Guangwu restored it and added authority over one province.

translations.literal: Twelve attendant clerks.
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve attendants.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：都官从事，主察举百官犯法者。

translations.literal: Original note says: Capital bureau attendant: in charge of investigating and reporting officials who violate the law.
translations.idiomatic: The capital-bureau attendant impeached metropolitan officials who broke the law.

sentences.zh: 功曹从事，主州选署及众事。

translations.literal: Merit bureau attendant: in charge of provincial selections and appointments and the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The merit clerk handled provincial appointments and general administration.

sentences.zh: 别驾从事，校尉行部则奉引，录众事。

translations.literal: Separate-car attendant: when the colonel inspects departments, then he leads the train and records the multitude of affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The separate-car attendant led the colonel's inspection tours and kept his records.

translations.literal: Ledger bureau attendant: in charge of ledgers of wealth, grain, and documents.
translations.idiomatic: The accounts clerk managed fiscal ledgers and grain registers.

sentences.zh: 其有军事，则置兵曹从事，主兵事。

translations.literal: If there is military affairs, then a military bureau attendant is established, in charge of military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In wartime a military-affairs clerk was added to the staff.

sentences.zh: 其餘部郡国从事，每郡国各一人，主督促文书，察举非法，皆州自辟除，故通為百石云。

translations.literal: As for the remaining department commandery-kingdom attendants, each commandery and kingdom each has one person, in charge of urging documents, investigating and reporting what is unlawful; all are personally recruited by the province; therefore collectively they are called one hundred piculs, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Each commandery and kingdom also had one provincial clerk to push paperwork and report abuses; provinces hired them locally, so they were loosely treated as hundred-picul posts.

translations.literal: Twenty-five deputy assistants.
translations.idiomatic: There were twenty-five subordinate aides.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主簿录阁下事，省文书。

translations.literal: Original note says: The chief clerk records affairs below the gate tower and examines documents.
translations.idiomatic: The chief clerk managed office business under the colonel and vetted correspondence.

translations.literal: Gate pavilion chief is in charge of provincial rectification.
translations.idiomatic: The gate chief enforced provincial discipline at headquarters.

translations.literal: Gate merit bureau document assistant is in charge of selection and appointment.
translations.idiomatic: The merit clerk's aide handled personnel selection.

translations.literal: Master of the Classic of Filial Piety is in charge of supervising examination of the classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Classic of Filial Piety instructor supervised classical examinations.

translations.literal: Master of the Monthly Ordinances is in charge of seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: The Monthly Ordinances specialist oversaw seasonal temple rites.

translations.literal: Master of statutes and ordinances is in charge of leveling the laws.
translations.idiomatic: The statute specialist advised on legal interpretation.

translations.literal: Ledger bureau document assistant is in charge of ledgers and documents.
translations.idiomatic: The accounts clerk's aide kept the ledgers.

sentences.zh: 其余都官书佐及每郡国，各有典郡书佐一人，各主一郡文书，以郡吏补，岁满一更。

translations.literal: As for the remaining capital bureau document assistants and for each commandery and kingdom, each has one commandery classic document assistant, each in charge of one commandery's documents; they are filled from commandery clerks; when the year is full, one rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Each commandery also supplied a resident clerk for its documents, rotated annually from local officials.

translations.literal: The colonel director of retainers' department commanderies are seven.
translations.idiomatic: The colonel director of retainers oversaw seven commanderies.

sentences.zh: 河南尹一人，主京都，特奉朝请。

translations.literal: One governor of Henan, in charge of the capital metropolis, specially granted court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The governor of Henan ran the capital and held standing right to imperial audience.

sentences.zh: 其京兆尹、左冯翊、右扶风三人，汉初都长安，皆秩中二千石，谓之三辅。

translations.literal: As for the governor of the capital district, left Fengyi, and right Fufeng, three persons—at the beginning of Han the capital was at Chang'an; all ranks were middle two thousand piculs; they are called the three auxiliaries.
translations.idiomatic: The metropolitan governor and the two flank commanderies around Chang'an had each ranked at two thousand piculs middle rate and were called the Three Guardians of the capital.

sentences.zh: 中兴都雒阳，更以河南郡为尹，以三辅陵庙所在，不改其号，但减其秩。

translations.literal: At the restoration the capital was Luoyang; Henan commandery was changed to governor; because the three auxiliaries were where mausolea and temples were located, their titles were not changed, but only their rank was reduced.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang Henan became a metropolitan governorship; the old Three Guardians kept their names to tend western tombs but were demoted in salary.

sentences.zh: 其餘弘农、河内、河东三郡。

translations.literal: The remainder: Hongnong, Henei, Hedong, three commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: The other three commanderies in his circuit were Hongnong, Henei, and Hedong.

sentences.zh: 其置尹，冯翊、扶风及太守丞奉之本位，在《地理志》。

translations.literal: As for the establishment of governors, Fengyi, Fufeng, and the fundamental positions of grand administrators and assistants are in the Treatise on Geography.
translations.idiomatic: The full tables for metropolitan governors, Fengyi, Fufeng, and county magistrates appear in the Treatise on Geography.
